items.title: [field] Sync filled state after native form reset

labels.name: component: field
labels.description: Changes related to the field component.

items.body:
Fixes #5765.

Sync `Field.Control` and `Input` filled state with the native value after form reset. Covers nonempty defaults, canceled resets, external forms, controlled values, and an input replaced by a reset handler without emitting `onValueChange`.

Validation passed: related jsdom tests (1,145), Field/Input/Form browser tests in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit (342 per engine), `pnpm typescript`, `pnpm eslint`, `pnpm stylelint`, and `pnpm prettier`. The reset regression tests fail on the unchanged base.

- [x] I have followed (at least) the [PR section of the contributing guide](https://github.com/mui/base-ui/blob/HEAD/CONTRIBUTING.md#sending-a-pull-request).

items.title: [field] FieldControl warns about a changing defaultValue that it already handles correctly

labels.name: status: waiting for maintainer
labels.description: These issues haven't been looked at yet by a maintainer.

items.body:
# Bug report

## Current behavior

`Field.Control` / `Input` log a dev warning whenever `defaultValue` changes after mount:

> Base UI: A component is changing the default value state of an uncontrolled FieldControl after being initialized. To suppress this warning opt to use a controlled FieldControl.

The warning comes from `useControlled({ default: defaultValue })`. But for an uncontrolled field, `FieldControl` doesn't use the hook's stored value: it spreads the *current* `defaultValue` prop onto the native `<input>` (`...(isControlled ? { value } : { defaultValue })`). React DOM therefore keeps the input's `defaultValue` up to date, and `form.reset()` (including React 19's automatic reset after a form action) restores the latest default, exactly as with a native `<input>`. The behaviour is correct; only the warning is wrong.

A real use for a changing `defaultValue`: pointing it at a draft of what the user typed, so that the reset React performs after a form action returns (for example, a server-side validation refusal) doesn't wipe the user's input.

## Expected behavior

No warning, since `FieldControl` handles a changing `defaultValue` correctly for uncontrolled fields. Same as a native `<input>`, which logs nothing for the same code.

## Reproducible example

```tsx
'use client'
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Input } from '@base-ui/react/input'

export default function Repro() {
  const [draft, setDraft] = useState<string | null>(null)
  return (
    <form
      onChange={(e) => setDraft(String(new FormData(e.currentTarget).get('name')))}
      action={async () => {
        // a refusal: the form stays open, and React resets it
      }}
    >
      <Input name="name" defaultValue={draft ?? 'Stored'} />
      <button type="submit">Save</button>
    </form>
  )
}
```

Type into the field: the warning is logged on the first keystroke. Submit: the typed value survives React's reset (correct). Swapping `Input` for a plain `<input>` keeps the identical behaviour with no warning.

## Base UI version

v1.7.0 (`@base-ui/utils` 0.3.2). I also checked v1.8.0 / `@base-ui/utils` 0.4.0: the check and `FieldControl`'s forwarding are unchanged.

## Which browser are you using?

Chrome; also reproduced in jsdom under Vitest.

## Which OS are you using?

macOS

## Additional context

Possible fixes: skip the default-value check for `FieldControl`'s `useControlled` call, since the component forwards the live `defaultValue` itself, or give `useControlled` an option to opt out of that check.

Related but distinct: #4451 (the same check throwing on circular values in Select).

items.title: [internal] Improve state initialization and add tests for React 17 fallback
items.body:
Issue described in https://github.com/mui/base-ui/pull/5462#issuecomment-5313700120 is actually not specific to `TabsPanel`, it is a global issue. hence fixed in `useId` instead of patching as suggested by `codex review`.

## Issue

On React 17, a component that mounted with an `id` prop kept that id forever, removing the prop never fell back to a generated one, because the fallback stored the caller's id in the slot meant for generated ids. Also switches `||` to `??` so an empty-string `id` is respected.

New `useId.react17.test.tsx` forces the fallback branch (mocks `SafeReact.useId` to `undefined`), which nothing tested before since the repo runs React 19 and CI's oldest job is React 18.

items.title: [field] Sync controlled value changes with field state

labels.name: component: field
labels.description: Changes related to the field component.

items.body:
`Field.Control` was the only Field control that ignored controlled value changes. Switch, Checkbox, Checkbox Group, Radio Group, Select, Slider, Combobox, Number Field, and OTP Field all sync through `useValueChanged` already. `Field.Control` instead drove every field concern from the DOM change event, so a value set from code had no path at all.

Two bugs followed.

**Dirty state never cleared for non-string values.** The dirty check compares the input's string value against a baseline captured from the `value` prop. With `value={5}` the baseline was the number `5`, so `"5" !== 5` held forever and `data-dirty` stayed set even after the user returned the field to its initial value. Array values failed the same way by reference. The control now registers the serialized value, so the baseline and the comparison agree.

**Programmatic changes left the field stale.** Setting the value from code, such as a clear button or a form library reset, updated the input text but not filled, dirty, or validity, so a resolved error stayed visible and a pending async validator for the old value could still publish.

The fix gives each mode one owner instead of running two sync paths at once. `useValueChanged` owns the controlled path, `onChange` owns the uncontrolled path, and `onChange` returns early when controlled. `Field.Control` now has the same shape as its siblings, with the residual difference being the mount-time DOM read that its uncontrolled mode requires.

Two smaller fixes ride along:

- `details.cancel()` in `onValueChange` now stops the internal handling. It was ignored.
- A controlled value the consumer rejects or rewrites no longer reaches the field state, matching Combobox, Number Field and OTP Field.

## Performance

Renders per keystroke for a controlled input, counted in jsdom (mount, then four keystrokes):

| Validation mode | Base | This PR | Number Field |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `onSubmit` | 1 per keystroke | 2 on the first, then 1 | 2 on the first, then 1 |
| `onChange` | 1 per keystroke | 2 per keystroke | 2 per keystroke |

Moving the work into a layout effect costs one extra render per keystroke in `onChange` mode. That is the cost every sibling control already pays, and `Field.Control` now matches Number Field exactly. The base column achieved one render by doing the work synchronously in the change handler, which is the second sync path this PR removes.

labels.name: component: field
labels.description: Changes related to the field component.

items.body:
Two field lifecycle fixes. The blur half is a regression from #5460; the filled half predates it.

- **Controlled blur normalization no longer discards validation.** With `validationMode="onBlur"`, a blur handler that normalizes the controlled value (e.g. `.trim()`) had its commit retired by the value's prop transition. The blur handler now re-commits the settled DOM value in a microtask, unless it settled back to the initial value (a programmatic reset stays quiet). Async normalization after blur is still not covered.
- **`filled` is now derived from the current value** in a layout effect (the `NumberField` pattern) instead of transition callbacks and write-only mount effects. This fixes stale `data-filled` on remounts and custom `render` elements in `Field.Control`, `Checkbox.Root`, and `Switch.Root`, and `CheckboxGroup` now fully owns the filled state.

`dirty` stays transition-driven: deriving it needs mount-time `initialValue` ordering guarantees and interacts with #5345.
